checklist.title: TRIPOD+AI checklist for the reporting of prediction model studies
checklist.citation: Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, et al. TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods. BMJ 2024;385:e078378. doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-078378

items.text: Describe how the data were used (eg, for development and evaluation of model performance) in the analysis, including whether the data were partitioned, considering any sample size requirements

where.quote: The analysis was declared for `prediction`: models are judged on rows they never saw.

No rows were held out; performance was estimated by `5`-fold cross-validation (seed `0`); models were compared with each other and with the no-predictor baseline on `5`-fold cross-validation repeated `10` times (`5` where `5,000` or more rows train), by the corrected repeated k-fold t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004); R² was measured against the training rows' mean and pooled over every out-of-fold prediction.

items.note: answered in the bundle

items.text: Depending on the type of model, describe how predictors were handled in the analyses (functional form, rescaling, transformation, or any standardisation)

where.quote: Figure 2. Column lineage, from the 2 raw columns the analysis reads to the 2 columns of the model matrix (90 rows), through the steps every model family shares; a family's own steps (scaling, a spline basis) are in the methods. Line styles: solid, kept as it is. Drawn from the decision record.

items.note: answered in the bundle

items.text: Specify the type of model, rationale†, all model building steps, including any hyperparameter tuning, and method for internal validation

where.quote: No rows were held out; performance was estimated by `5`-fold cross-validation (seed `0`); models were compared with each other and with the no-predictor baseline on `5`-fold cross-validation repeated `10` times (`5` where `5,000` or more rows train), by the corrected repeated k-fold t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004); R² was measured against the training rows' mean and pooled over every out-of-fold prediction.

Two model families were chosen: linear regression and elastic net; with no rows held out, the choice among them is corrected by bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation (Tsamardinos et al. 2018), and that selection-corrected estimate is the reported result, not the best family's own score.

Two model families were chosen: linear regression and elastic net; with no rows held out, the choice among them is corrected by bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation (Tsamardinos et al. 2018), and that selection-corrected estimate is the reported result, not the best family's own score.
plan.text: This is the analysis as declared in TurboTab for prediction, through the decision recorded on 2026-11-04 at 13:44:52.021324 UTC. Under prediction no plan is locked: the held-out rows are the seal, and a family's score is the result only as the fit declares it (the held-out score of a family declared final before they were opened, or the selection-corrected estimate). It records what was declared in the software and when; it is not a registration with any outside registry, and the analyst may have seen the data. Its SHA-256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces, UTF-8) is 2a022e08fdcaf2d07c48f4699de8b09ecae69aefc52186e504553fe647ec3675: the same decisions give the same bytes, so the hash can be cited in an external registration.
